ateret-zekenim/2:_: And one does not say Tachanun on it: the custom of Eretz Yisrael is to go on Lag BaOmer to the graves of Rashbi and R. Elazar his son; and R. Eliezer HaLevi testified that he was always accustomed to say Nachem in Birkat Tishkon, and when he finished prayer R. Yitzchak Luria z"l told him from Rashbi buried there that he said: tell this man why does he say Nachem on the day of my joy — therefore he will be in nachem soon; and so it was that his eldest son died (nevertheless this was the intention of the Ari z"l) — behold one should not say supplication on this day.
biur-halacha/2:_: They are not allowed to circumvent, and so on, they are not allowed to be excavated in the field, and they are not allowed to be exalted
biur-halacha/3:_: Some practice, etc., and they err — explanation of the matter: there are three views here, and we will explain two of them that the poskim ruled for practical halachah. First view: the students of R' Akiva died for 34 days; proof from the Midrash that they died from Pesach until "kneading" of Shavuos, which is 15 days before Shavuos; when you remove 15 days from 49, 34 full days remain that they died — only that part of the day is like the whole day; therefore they get a haircut on the 34th day in the morning, and likewise marrying a woman is permitted from then on; this is the Mechaber's view in seifim 1 and 2. However per Rama there in seif 2 it implies he holds they ceased dying on the 33rd day, as the Gra wrote there — part of the day is like the whole day; per this view the custom not to get a haircut from Pesach until the morning of the 33rd, and from then until Shavuos, is permitted. Second view: what is said in the name of Tosafot — the students of R' Akiva died 33 full days, meaning on a day when Tachanun is not said they did not die; if so, when you remove seven days of Pesach — from the second day of Pesach — and another six Shabbosos and two days of Rosh Chodesh Iyar and day 1 when they did not die, behold 33 full days remain that they died; per this they died until Shavuos. Israel accepted upon themselves partial mourning for 33 days corresponding to those 33 days (except that one day may be eased with part of the day like the whole day, and they chose Lag BaOmer — perhaps for some reason, Peri Megadim) regarding counting and marriage — meaning to deduct from the 49 days of the Omer the first 16 days, from the second day of Pesach until the second day of Rosh Chodesh Iyar; those days they are lenient, and 33 full days remain until Shavuos on which they mourn; per this, those who get a haircut from Lag BaOmer onward and also on Rosh Chodesh Iyar err, for there are not 33 days — this is the Mechaber's intent.
chatam-sofer/1:_: There. {Rama: However if it falls, etc.} NB: see what is written in Knesset HaGedolah on this siman; nevertheless I did not be lenient and I forbade on erev Shavuos when it fell on Sunday to shave on the erev Shabbos before it, even though there is room to distinguish; requires study. Likewise milah on Sunday — I did not permit on the sixth day before it, for it is not comparable to the above, since it is only his Yom Tov and not for the majority of the community. Lag BaOmer on erev Shabbos — it is good to make marriages at night from the day of erev Shabbos and to consummate on Shabbos night, as Eliyah Rabbah's intent.
chatam-sofer/2:_: In the Mechaber seif 3 in gloss: on Lag BaOmer. Note: see responsa Chatam Sofer Orach Chayim siman 142 [there he brought the proclamation text announced in his community K"K P"B from the Gaon Moharar David Meshulam z"l, stating: since they practiced here to marry on Rosh Chodesh Iyar and Lag BaOmer and also marry during the three days of restriction, which is two contradictory things — therefore from now on it shall be fixed law to forbid weddings during the three restriction days; he wrote on this that it appears from these words they were strict only about the custom of marrying on these two times, which are two contradictory things in one place, as is understood in a large community where each year there will be two weddings on those times; but possibly in a small place where weddings are few, if a wedding occurs on Rosh Chodesh Iyar it may not occur during restriction days — then there is not two contradictions in one place; and possibly there is not so much strictness — see there well in all words of the responsum].
chatam-sofer/3:_: (There in Magen Avraham s.k. 6) s.v. "And he answered," etc. NB: see responsa Me'il Tzedakah:
chatam-sofer/4:_: (There in Magen Avraham s.k. 6) Rif and Rosh did not write. NB: it appears to me from the verse "and he was gathered" as in Chagigah daf 26a:
chokhmat-shlomo/2:_: Seif 2. {Rama: However if it falls on Sunday they practice to get a haircut on Friday for honor of Shabbos.} NB: behold if Rosh Chodesh Sivan falls on Sunday — whether it is permitted to get a haircut on erev Shabbos. I saw in Peri Megadim who wrote it is permitted, as on Lag BaOmer; and he wondered on Peri Chadash who forbids when Rosh Chodesh Iyar falls on Sunday to get a haircut on Friday, and wrote he did not know his reason, see there. It appears to me regarding Rosh Chodesh Sivan Peri Megadim's words are certainly not correct, for there is no proof from Lag BaOmer — there, since if he does not get a haircut on Lag BaOmer he cannot afterward even for the coming Shabbos, therefore we are concerned for disgrace for two Shabbosos; and on Lag BaOmer itself, since it is one day, we are concerned for oness and the like; especially since it is a disgrace that on Shabbos he does not shave and on Sunday after Shabbos he shaves — therefore permitted to shave on erev Shabbos; especially that not for this Shabbos they were concerned, since on it they forbade shaving and we are not concerned for his disgrace; but for the coming Shabbos we are concerned, since on it they permitted shaving before on Lag BaOmer and he will not be disgraced on Shabbos; and if he does not shave now, perhaps on Lag BaOmer an oness will be born for him and the like, and also disgrace for Shabbos as above — therefore they permitted shaving on erev Shabbos. But on Rosh Chodesh Sivan he can shave afterward for a long time — they were not concerned for oness; he can shave close to the coming Shabbos and will not be disgraced; and for that Shabbos alone there is no shaving, for on it they were not concerned for disgrace, since they forbade shaving until Rosh Chodesh whenever it falls. Further, on Lag BaOmer, which itself is permitted by law for most poskim — if it falls on Sunday, permitted adjacent to it. But on Rosh Chodesh Sivan it is explicit in Magen Avraham there is no leniency except on the three days of restriction; Peri Megadim himself wrote he did not know whence the custom to permit on Rosh Chodesh derives — if so, do not add to it: specifically on Rosh Chodesh, but not to permit even before it. This is Peri Chadash's reason: since on Rosh Chodesh Iyar most forbid and the Mechaber wrote it is an error in their hands — therefore even those who are lenient mean on Rosh Chodesh itself and not to be lenient even before it; it is not comparable to Lag BaOmer where most poskim permit, as above. Therefore both on Rosh Chodesh Iyar and Rosh Chodesh Sivan one should forbid shaving on erev Shabbos — so it appears correct for practical halachah:
dagul-merevavah/1:_: Rama: and a groom on the Shabbos before his wedding that they call "Shabbos of the groom" — see below siman 551 in Magen Avraham s.k. 6; nevertheless regarding sefirah and especially after Lag BaOmer, it appears to me to permit on erev Shabbos of the Shabbos they call "Shabbos of the groom":
eliyah-rabbah/1:_: [א] [Levush] And the reason etc. In Shibbolei HaLeket and Tannaita they wrote the reason that the judgment of the wicked in Gehinnom is twelve months, and R. Yochanan ben Nuri said from Passover until Shavuot, as it says "from the time of Shabbat on its Shabbat"; and in Sefer Adam veChavah p. 44 he wrote that because they are days of judgment, for the omer comes from barley; accordingly it would be fit to forbid even on Lag BaOmer, and I wrote in Eliyahu Zuta that it appears from this reason of Maharil that he practices for himself not to cut until erev Shavuot, and so in Maaglei Tzedek — except they were lenient.
eliyah-rabbah/2:_: (b) But to Belarus and so on. And it is permissible to make an engagement meal at the same time, meaning that no dancing is permitted, but in the kitten is forbidden to dance and consist of permission, who is up to the head of the month of Air, and from the beginning of the month of Sivan to weeks must be satisfied if the dance and responsibility of the Authority should be facilitated:
eliyah-rabbah/3:_: There is no punishment and so on. For it is thought that an adopted person is doing, but someone who improves them (the Great Church):
eliyah-rabbah/4:_: [4] [Levush] To marry a woman. Likewise one may not learn from this to places that practice getting a haircut until Rosh Chodesh Iyar that marriage is permitted, for marriage is more stringent — they practice in all places; and this case is different after Lag BaOmer, when they ceased dying — not like Bach (Mahari Weil), and requires study; in Shibulei HaLeket and Tanya they wrote some places practice marrying until Rosh Chodesh Iyar. I heard the Gaon my grandfather, may his memory be for a blessing, did not wish to permit making marriages on Rosh Chodesh Iyar that fell on Shabbos, even though Bach permits:
eshel-avraham/1:_: The custom in ShL and Tannaita — they wrote the reason that judgment of the wicked in Gehinnom is twelve months, and R. Yochanan ben Nuri says from Passover until Shavuot; and in Sefer Adam veChavah the reason is because they are days of judgment, for the omer comes from barley; and for this reason Maharil practiced not to cut until erev Shavuot.
eshel-avraham/2:_: Permitted. But a baal brit may not get a haircut within thirty — responsa of Maharitz and Maharam; see responsa Mahari Weil siman 26:
kaf-hachayyim/1:_: (b) It is customary not to marry a woman and so on in all places. column. Dressed. B.C.
kaf-hachayyim/2:_: (b) There. Not to marry a woman, etc. — it is implied from the plain sense of Shulchan Aruch's words that there is no distinction between marriage of mitzvah — such as when he has no wife and children — and marriage that is not of mitzvah. So too Ohr Sameach letter 1; so too Zarua Orach Chayyim siman 68: even where most are not careful about haircutting on these days, one may not permit marrying during the Omer for one who did not fulfill peru urvu, for marriage is more stringent for them than haircutting, since we have not seen they practiced leniency except in haircutting, see there. Bach on the Mechaber letter 1 wrote: although Maharam Lonzano and Peri Chadash permitted marrying a woman for one who did not fulfill peru urvu, and their reasons and rationales are with them — nevertheless the widespread custom is not to marry at all until Lag BaOmer, end of his words. So too Knesset HaGedolah in Hagahot Taz on Maharam's words — we do not practice thus. So too Ohr Sameach there. R' Zalman letter 3; Mishna Berurah letter 1; see Shevut Yaakov vol. 2 siman 35, who wrote that once a certain scholar was lenient regarding marriage during the days of counting against the custom and their match did not succeed well; therefore he wrote one who guards his soul should distance himself from marriage on such days even if there are many sides to be lenient, for danger is more stringent than prohibition, and not to nullify the custom publicly, end of his words; see below letter 12.
kaf-hachayyim/3:_: (c) there. Not to marry a woman and so on and like an old widow who wants to marry an old widowed woman. The Holy One. O’A and his divorce from the marriage in every guerna, Shari, there is joy, and as a result of his wife, C. S. B.C., from the R&D. Joseph O’A., who is finally a member of the world. from “B” or “A.”.
kaf-hachayyim/4:_: (d) There. Not to marry a woman, etc. — the reason not to increase joy is because at that time the students of R' Akiva died. Tur. Nevertheless the blessing shehecheyanu is permitted to say on these days from Pesach until Lag BaOmer; and although it is written below siman 551 seif 17 it is good to be careful not to say shehecheyanu between the straits, etc. — that is different, destruction of the Temple, which is more stringent for us than saying amen, letter 2; and there is no distinction between fruit and garment; so too Ikvei HaDat siman 21, see there. Yafeh Lelev ch. 3 letter 3; so they teach in my yeshiva; and we are not concerned for what is written in Melach siman 6 letter 12 — good custom not to put on a new garment, etc. between Pesach and Lag BaOmer, see there.
levushei-serad/1:_: A.C. will not betray and so on. Same as C.M.:
netiv-chayim/1:_: (Magen Avraham s.k. 6) And regarding a matter that can be attributed to lack of intent for prohibition — NB: I wonder if this came from his mouth; behold regarding haircutting, if part of one place get a haircut until Rosh Chodesh Iyar and some from Lag BaOmer onward, it is obvious it is "do not cut yourselves," even per the first answer that answers regarding work it is not "do not cut yourselves" — one says work is lacking for him — for some contradict others in one city; behold according to all one must practice prohibition for 33 days, and here there are not 33 and here there are not 33. Also what he wrote that for Rava's conclusion we do not divide this view of "one who sees says," etc. — in truth for the conclusion too the Talmud's view fits the correct view, for it says three learn from it that they acted per their words, and it does not say learn from this that the plaster decreased or the beam shook; rather because it can be rejected — "one who sees says" — he aerates the air or he aerates water; so Maharshal in Yesh Seder end of chapter 5, see there:
rabbi-akiva-eiger/3:_: Seif 3 in the gloss: to get a haircut from Lag BaOmer onward; but one who completed thirty-day mourning on day 34 of the Omer — see responsa Devar Moshe siman 32:
rabbi-akiva-eiger/2:_: Magen Avraham s.k. 6: if so regarding haircutting too one may say "one who sees." Simply: since those who haircut until Rosh Chodesh Iyar may not from Lag BaOmer onward, and those from Lag BaOmer onward are forbidden before Rosh Chodesh — if some until Rosh Chodesh Iyar and some from Lag BaOmer, this is "do not cut yourselves." So responsa Me'il Tzedakah siman 49; see there also siman 2 and responsa Tamim De'im siman 168–170:
shaarei-teshuvah/1:_: To marry — Avnei Nezer and Machatzit HaShekel wrote the widespread custom is not to marry at all even if he did not fulfill peru urvu; one does not marry until Lag BaOmer; see there in name of Zer'a Emet that even where most are not careful about haircutting, nevertheless one may not permit marrying, see there; see below s.k. 3 in name of Shevut Yaakov; see Pri HaAdamah ch. 3 daf 48 — an incident in Jerusalem to be stringent not to marry a woman on Rosh Chodesh during Omer days even a widower with a widow, see there; see responsa Chinuch Beit Yosef siman 21 who permitted in time of pressing need for one who came from elsewhere to marry on Lag BaOmer, became ill, recovered after Lag BaOmer, very necessary for his household, and she does not wish to move without marriage, and he is still somewhat ill with no attendant here at the fair, and the match may be voided by this gift that he will part ways, etc.; therefore he permitted marriage combined with leniency that some places practice permitting marriage after Lag BaOmer, see there:
yad-ephraim/1:_: In Taz s.k. 1: and on two days of Rosh Chodesh mourning does not apply — they practiced leniency there; this is all automatic — all 33 days forbidden to haircut, all as it should be:
yad-ephraim/2:_: (Psalm) and in the words of our custom to the last of all things:
